title: Cadillac Mines Corporation Files Final Prospectus and Announces Pricing and Upsizing of Initial Public Offering to $385 Million
author: Na
description: Cadillac Mines Corporation successfully priced and upsized its IPO to $385 million, offering 47.1 million common shares at $6.90 per share and 6.3 million flow-through shares at $9.52 per share. The offering was increased from the initial $363 million due to excess demand. The company also secured a $60 million private placement from Agnico Eagle Mines. Trading on the TSX is expected to begin July 24, 2026 under the symbol 'CADY', with closing expected August 5, 2026.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Agnico Eagle's $60 million investment in Cadillac Mines represents a strategic investment decision but is not material enough to significantly impact Agnico's overall business. The investment indicates confidence in Cadillac's projects but does not constitute major news for Agnico itself.

title: Cadillac Mines Corporation dépose un prospectus définitif et annonce le prix de son premier appel public à l’épargne qui a été majoré à 385 M$
author: Na
description: Cadillac Mines Corporation announced its initial public offering priced at $385 million, upsized from the initially planned $363 million due to strong demand. The offering includes 47.075 million common shares at $6.90 each and 6.303 million flow-through shares at $9.52 each. Agnico Eagle Mines will subscribe for 8.696 million common shares in a concurrent private placement for approximately $60 million. Trading on the TSX under symbol 'CADY' is expected to commence July 24, 2026, with closing anticipated for August 5, 2026.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Agnico Eagle Mines' decision to invest approximately $60 million in Cadillac Mines through a private placement demonstrates confidence in the company's exploration potential and strategic value along the Cadillac-Larder Lake fault, a prolific mining region.

title: Is It Better to Play the Historic Gold Rally With a Physical Gold or Mining Stock ETF in 2026?
author: Brendan Coffey
description: The article compares two gold investment approaches: SPDR Gold Shares (GLD), which tracks physical gold bullion with lower volatility and fees, versus VanEck Gold Miners ETF (GDX), which invests in mining company stocks with higher returns but greater risk. While GLD offers stability and lower costs, GDX is recommended as the better buy for 2026 due to superior long-term performance, operating leverage benefits during gold rallies, and dividend payments, despite its higher volatility.

title: SLV vs SGDM: Is a Silver ETF Better Than a Gold Miner Fund to Ride the Commodity Boom in 2026?
author: Brendan Coffey
description: The article compares iShares Silver Trust (SLV) and Sprott Gold Miners ETF (SGDM) as investment vehicles for precious metals exposure. SLV offers direct physical silver bullion exposure with a 58.7% 1-year return, while SGDM provides indirect gold exposure through mining equities with a 40.1% 1-year return. The author recommends SGDM due to its lower expense ratio (0.46% vs 0.50%), dividend income, and more favorable tax treatment compared to SLV's collectibles tax classification.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: SGDM is recommended as the better choice due to lower expense ratio (0.46%), dividend income (1.10% yield), more favorable tax treatment, and operational leverage that allows miners to profit disproportionately as gold prices rise. Long-term annualized returns (16%) are comparable to SLV with less volatility.

title: Gold Miners or Silver Miners: Which Precious Metals ETF Is the Better Buy Right Now?
author: Sara Appino
description: The article compares two precious metals mining ETFs: Sprott Gold Miners ETF (SGDM), which focuses on North American gold producers with a lower 0.46% expense ratio, and Global X Silver Miners ETF (SIL), which provides global silver exposure with higher 1-year returns (83% vs 53%) but greater volatility. Gold miners are recommended for new precious metals investors, while silver miners suit those seeking higher-conviction bets on industrial and monetary demand convergence.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Lower expense ratio (0.46%), more stable with lower beta (0.53) and maximum drawdown (45%), better 5-year growth ($2,214 from $1,000), and recommended as the more established entry point for new precious metals investors.

Higher 1-year returns (83%), higher dividend yield (1.10%), and positioned as a higher-conviction bet for investors with existing precious metals exposure seeking exposure to industrial demand and green transition themes.
